description: GWHAT is the Ground-Water Hydrograph Analysis Toolbox maintained by Jean-Sébastien Gosselin and contributors. It interprets observation-well hydrographs with daily soil-moisture and aquifer-water budgets to estimate groundwater recharge in unconfined aquifers. A user supplies well levels, daily weather and site parameters; the program produces recharge estimates, tables and graphs for the weather-data period. Geographic coverage is each configured aquifer site, and a hydrograph longer than five years provides stronger constraints according to the README. The suite also computes well barometric response when pressure and earth-tide data are available. GPL-3.0 source and release packages are public. A limitation is that an inferred recharge series depends on aquifer type and input quality; the method cannot be applied unchanged to a confined well. GWHAT can inform groundwater supply and drought stress studies. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis is a separate candidate weather reference, not a measured well record. No hydrograph or executable was downloaded.
